title: The Spatial Turn in Protected Area Governance: An Actor-Network Analysis of Nature Education and Community Co-Construction in Qi’ao Island Mangroves, China
content: Protected areas rely on boundary demarcation and regulation to safeguard ecosystems, yet these measures often sever communities' long-standing ties to land and intensify conservation–livelihood tensions. Existing research emphasises technical management or community co-management, but formal participatory channels often reduce resident involvement to rhetoric and leave the role of space under-examined. Drawing on three years of engaged fieldwork (2022–2025) at the Qi'ao–Dangan Provincial Nature Reserve, Zhuhai, this study traces an unanticipated outcome: a multi-actor network built around nature education self-organised after the team withdrew. Combining actor-network theory with discourse-coalition analysis, we analyse semi-structured interviews, participant observation, policy documents and field memos. Boardwalks, village lecture venues and educational trails are not neutral artefacts: competing and hybridising discourses unfold alongside spatial reorganisation, and space and discourse are mutually constituted, with discourse gaining material anchors through spatial configuration and sites acquiring governance meaning through framing. Nature education operates as a contact zone that activates space as a medium of translation and converts policy rhetoric into practical governance order. The paper advances a spatial-turn thesis: treating space as a passive background container helps explain why participation often fails, and identifies conditions under which substantive co-construction may emerge in mangrove protected areas.
